拓.meaning: A sailor wants a garden on a rocky island. He ties his <part>anchor</part> to a rope and swings it like a hammer, smashing each <part>stone</part> to gravel and dragging the bits into the sea. By autumn there's bare earth for carrots. It took a year to <kanji>clear</kanji> the land.
拓.on: He celebrates with a crunchy <sound>taco</sound> on the first flat patch.
拓.kun: His wife cheers from the boat, kicking up one high <sound>hee</sound>l: '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

凶.meaning: In a quiet barbershop, a <part>bucket</part> of fresh flowers stands by the door. Every night someone sneaks in with a pair of <part>scissors</part> and snips the heads off. The barber sets a trap and catches him: the mayor, in a mask. A small but real <kanji>villain</kanji>.
凶.on: He tries to slip away on the train, shouting '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!' and stretching the start, but trips over the bucket.

抽.meaning: A dentist has lost her pliers, so she ties a tiny <part>anchor</part> to a string, hooks it round a crocodile's wobbly tooth and pulls. Out it pops, with a note stuck to it giving the <part>reason</part> for the ache: 'Too many sweets.' The oddest tooth she's had to <kanji>pluck</kanji>.
抽.on: The crocodile had been <sound>chew</sound>ing gum for a week, and it's still stuck to the tooth.
抽.kun: To say thanks, the crocodile hands her one high <sound>hee</sound>l and a <sound>key</sound> to the swamp.

抹.meaning: A ship's painter writes THE <part>end</part> in huge letters on the hull, then the captain says the voyage will go on. So the painter hangs off the <part>anchor</part> chain with a sponge and scrubs the letters away one by one. It takes him all night to <kanji>rub</kanji> them out.
抹.on: Two scruffy <sound>mutts</sound> on deck chase the soap bubbles he makes.

謡.meaning: A shy monk is asked to give a <part>speech</part> at a picnic, so he sings it instead, slow and low, tapping time with a <part>can opener</part> on the bean tins. The ants stop to listen and the ducks hum along. The whole picnic turns into a <kanji>chant</kanji>.
謡.on: A boy at the back keeps the beat with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo, up and down, slowly.
謡.kun: Afterwards everyone slurps <sound>u</sound>don from one big <sound>tu</sound>b.

腸.meaning: An astronaut on the <part>moon</part> eats a whole crate of space noodles under the <part>sunbeams</part>. Soon a long, twisty rumble travels round and round inside her belly, like a train in a tunnel. Mission control hears it on the radio and worries about her <kanji>intestines</kanji>.
腸.on: The doctor on the radio tells her to loosen her tight <sound>cho</sound>ker.
腸.kun: Back home she rests in a <sound>hu</sound>t, the crew cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!', a baby cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and she soaks in a warm <sound>tu</sound>b.

魅.meaning: A <part>ghost</part> haunts a young apple tree that has <part>not yet</part> grown its first fruit. Every night it sits in the branches, staring and waiting. Weeks pass. It forgets to rattle chains or scare anyone. A ghost that can't stop watching a tree: that's <kanji>fascination</kanji>.
魅.on: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands beside it, staring at the tree just as hard.
